claim.pdf_says: A file may be opened with the INPUT, OUTPUT, EXTEND, and I-O phrases in the same run unit. ... preceded by the execution of a CLOSE statement, without the LOCK phrase, for that file. (EXTEND, and 'without the LOCK phrase,' are boxed, with no square brackets)
claim.markdown_says: (5) A file may be opened with the INPUT, OUTPUT, [║EXTEND,║] and I-O phrases in the same run unit. ... a CLOSE statement, [║without the LOCK phrase,║] for that file.
claim.why_it_matters: Square brackets not printed in the standard were added around the boxed (high-subset) text; elsewhere the transcription marks boxed text with ║...║ alone, and the brackets read as an optionality notation the rule does not carry.

verdict.reasoning: The 300 dpi render of page 453 (VIII-23, Relative I-O OPEN GR5) shows 'EXTEND,' and 'without the LOCK phrase,' each enclosed in a plain rectangular box, with no square bracket glyphs before or after either box. The transcription's line 31 reads '[║EXTEND,║]' and '[║without the LOCK phrase,║]', so it adds brackets the page does not print. The transcription's own convention marks boxed text as ║...║ alone: about 490 such spans in specs/ANSI_COBOL_1985.md, against only 6 occurrences of '[║'. The brackets are therefore an added artifact. In prose they could be misread as COBOL optional-element notation. The words of the rule are unchanged, so the severity stays cosmetic.
